---
title: "Get started"
---

This guide sets up Positron Server on JupyterHub. You install two things in the
single-user environment: Positron Server itself, and `jupyter-positron-server`,
which adds a Positron tile to the JupyterLab launcher. Then you add Positron Server
to the session `PATH` and restart JupyterHub.

To skip these steps, use one of the [deployment templates](deployment.qmd). They
include an install script for The Littlest JupyterHub (TLJH) and a docker-compose
template.

::: callout-important
This guide applies to Positron Server 2026.09.0 and later, and to 2026.06.1 and
earlier. Versions 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 check the license differently and
need the [verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd). The
[version table](index.qmd#which-setup-applies-to-your-version) shows which guide
applies to each version.
:::

## Before you begin

You need a license file and the Positron Server download.

### Request a license file

Positron Server is free for educational use under the
[Positron Education License Rider](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/LICENSE.txt).
To request a license file (`license.lic`), send email to
[academic-licenses@posit.co](mailto:academic-licenses@posit.co). This file is the
only thing you need from Posit.

### Download Positron Server

Positron Server is available only as a Linux archive from the Posit content
delivery network (CDN). It does not appear on the Positron download page or on the
GitHub releases page. Download the build that matches the CPU architecture of your
single-user servers:

| Architecture | Download |
|---|---|
| x86_64 (Intel and AMD) | [positron-server-linux-x64-{{< var positron.version >}}.tar.gz]({{< var positron.url-x64 >}}) |
| ARM64 | [positron-server-linux-arm64-{{< var positron.version >}}.tar.gz]({{< var positron.url-arm64 >}}) |

To check the architecture, run `uname -m` on the server. The output `x86_64`
means the first row, and `aarch64` or `arm64` means the second row.

## Step 1: Install Positron Server in the single-user image {#install-positron-server}

Download Positron Server and unpack it into `/opt/positron-server`. For ARM64, use
the ARM64 link from the table above.

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
curl -L -o /tmp/positron-server.tar.gz {{< var positron.url-x64 >}}
mkdir -p /opt/positron-server
tar -xzf /tmp/positron-server.tar.gz -C /opt/positron-server --strip-components=1
```

Next, copy the license file into the activation directory, next to the bundled
`license-manager` binary. In the path below, replace `<arch>` with `x86_64` or
`aarch64`.

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
install -m 644 license.lic /opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic
```

::: callout-important
The license file needs mode `644`. Each session runs `positron-server` as the
student, and `positron-server` reads the license file itself. With a root-only
mode such as `600`, every session fails to start.
:::

Before you continue, confirm that `license-manager` accepts the license file:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license-manager status
```

## Step 2: Install jupyter-positron-server in the single-user image {#install-jupyter-positron-server}

Install `jupyter-positron-server` into the Python environment that runs the
single-user server. On TLJH, that environment is `/opt/tljh/user`:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/tljh/user/bin/pip install 'jupyter-positron-server>=0.0.6'
```

`jupyter-positron-server` is a jupyter-server-proxy extension. It adds the Positron
tile to the JupyterLab launcher, and starts Positron Server the first time a
student opens it.

## Step 3: Add Positron Server to the session PATH {#point-single-user-servers-at-positron-server}

JupyterHub starts each single-user server with the variables in
`c.Spawner.environment`. Add `/opt/positron-server/bin` to `PATH` there, so that
`jupyter-positron-server` can find `positron-server`:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import os

c.Spawner.environment = {
    "PATH": "/opt/positron-server/bin:" + os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"),
}
```

You do not need any license environment variables. Positron Server finds
`license.lic` in its activation directory.

## Step 4: Restart JupyterHub {#restart-jupyterhub}

Restart JupyterHub to load the configuration:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
systemctl restart jupyterhub
```

After the restart, students see a Positron tile in the JupyterLab launcher. To
open Positron instead of JupyterLab when students sign in, see
[Common settings](common_settings.qmd#start-students-in-positron-server).

## How it works

When a student selects the Positron tile, `jupyter-positron-server` starts
`positron-server` inside the single-user server of that student. Positron Server
checks `license.lic` before it starts, so a missing, expired, or altered license
file stops the session. When Positron Server is running, `jupyter-positron-server`
opens it in the browser with a connection token for that session.

[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) shows what each license failure looks like
in the logs.

## Move an existing deployment off the verifier

If you set up Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 with the signing key and
the Hub verifier service, you do not need either one after you upgrade to 2026.09.0
or later. To remove them, make these four changes:

1. Change the license file mode from `600` to `644`, so sessions can read it.
2. Remove `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` from `c.Spawner.environment`.
3. Remove the `positron-license` entry from `c.JupyterHub.services`, and the
   `positron-license-service` entry from `c.JupyterHub.load_roles`.
4. Delete the signing key at `/etc/positron/signing-key.pem`, and uninstall
   `jupyter-positron-verifier` from the Hub environment.
